chunks.text:
Presentation
Sneha Gavankar Good day and welcome to Tata Motors Limited Q2 FY27 Earnings Call. I have with me today Mr. Girish Wagh, Managing Director and CEO; Mr. GV Ramanan, CFO and the Investor Relations team. Today we'll walk you through the results presentation followed by Q&A. As a reminder, all participants will be in listen- only mode and we will be taking questions by the Teams platform. The same is already open to you for submitting questions. You are requested to mention your name and the name of your organization while submitting the questions. With that, I now hand over to Mr. GV Ramanan. Over to you. GV Ramanan Thank you, Sneha. Good evening and welcome to Tata Motors Q2 FY27 Earnings Call. Thank you for joining us today. I'll be taking you through our financial performance for the quarter and the half-year ended September 30, 2026. Safe harbour statement. This is the regular statement that we have given, and like last quarter, our primary numbers represent the standalone financials, which include the joint operations with Tata Cummins. Consolidated results follow later in the deck. There is no change in the reporting parameters versus this quarter. Freight Tiger continues to be consolidated as a subsidiary, as it was in Q1. With that, let me take you through the highlights of the call.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · RANJAN KUMAR
chunks.text:
On products, at Prawaas 5.0 we unveiled our next-generation passenger mobility solution, including the launch of new Ultra Prime and Starbus Prime range. We also showcased our next-gen aggregates portfolio at Bauma CONEXPO India 2026. We were crowned the Best Truck of the Year at the Logistics and Transport Award 2026 in the UAE, a recognition that comes alongside a very strong quarter of export, which I will cover under the volume section. Signed MoU with Drivn to offer innovative leasing and financing solutions for our electric commercial vehicles, easing the total cost of ownership conversation for fleet customers. We collaborated with Petronas to pilot a scalable used-oil recycling model, extending the circular economy work we began with HPCL last quarter. During the quarter, we also partnered with Welspun Renewable Energy to develop a 86-megawatt wind-solar hybrid project.
A quick update on IVECO transaction, which has progressed in line with the timeline we shared last quarter. We obtained all required regulatory clearances, completing the condition to launch the offer. Consequently, the acceptance period opened on 7 September 2026 and will close on 26 October 2026. On 9 October, we increased the offer price from EUR14.10 to EUR14.40 per share in consideration of the slight

On 16 October, IVECO EGM approved all offer-related resolutions. As of 22 October, approximately 35% of shares have been tendered. As typically seen in the tender offer process, a significant portion of shares tend to be tendered towards the very end of the acceptance period, particularly in the final 24 to 48 hours. We therefore remain confident of a successful completion of the open offer. Subject to the offer conditions being met, settlement is expected on 30 October 2026, when Tata Motors will pay the offer price for the shares tendered. We will come back to you with an update on IVECO once the offer is settled.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · RANJAN KUMAR
chunks.text: Q2 wholesales were at 1,35,100 units, up 42% year-on-year and up 24% sequentially. Growth was once again broad-based, with every segment in double digits. HCV was up 41%, ILMCV was up 24%, small commercial cargo and pickup was up 27%, CV passenger up 31%, and international business was up 177%, close to 2.6 times over last year. The step up in international business that you see is driven by the Indonesian order, where deliveries ramped up sharply during the quarter on top of the steady export trajectory we built through FY26. For the half year, wholesales were at 2,43,800 units, up 35%. HCV up 32%, ILMCV up 20%, small commercial pickup, again a double-digit growth of 30%, and CV passenger was up 26%, and the international business was up 114%.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · RANJAN KUMAR
chunks.text: The next few slides cover the standalone business, including the joint operations with Tata Cummins. The Financial Highlight. This slide summarizes the standalone financials, including the joint operations with Cummins. Volume momentum translated into 42% revenue growth. Revenue for Q2 was ₹23,900 crores. EBITDA was about ₹2,800 crores, up 31% at a margin of 11.7%. While EBITDA margin was down 90 basis points YoY, it held flat sequentially despite a commodity headwind intensifying further during the quarter. I will take you through the margin walk later. EBIT margin was at 9.7%, down 50 basis points YoY. EBIT at ₹2,300 crores. The profit before tax, before exceptional items, was at ₹2,700 crores, up 51%. So, an absolute profit growth has again outpaced volume growth. Free cash flow was at ₹4,600 crores against ₹2,200 crores in Q2 last year, an improvement of ₹2,400 crore, which I'll walk you through shortly. With that, the net cash stood at ₹11,300 crores as at September 30 against ₹7,500 crores at March and ₹7,100 crores at June end, and this is after the dividend payout in Q1. The Auto ROCE was 65% on a trailing 12-month basis against 68% at the end of Q1, a moderation largely reflecting the lower margins over the last 12 months. Investment spends was ₹600 crore for the quarter against ₹700 crore in Q2 last year, and this is in line with the plan.

Coming to the Q2 EBIT walk. This is the walk from PBT before exceptional items of ₹1,757 crores in Q2 FY26 to ₹2,660 crores in Q2 FY27, with the EBIT margins bridge shown underneath. Volume and mix contributed to around ₹1,159 crore, with an improved net realization of further ₹1,017 crores. Together, these added 230 basis points to EBIT margin. Variable cost, with the principal headwinds at ₹1,416 crore, 590 basis point impact. This is the commodity inflation which was flowing into the material cost. Other cost contributed positively at 280 bps. Even though they were higher in absolute terms by ₹214 crores,

depreciation, product development were favourable by ₹13 crores, employee cost was higher by ₹88 crores, and other expenses by ₹139 crores. This is operating leverage on a 42% larger revenue base. FX and other items added 30 basis points, or ₹350 crores. chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · RANJAN KUMAR
chunks.text: Coming to the free cash flow for the quarter, FCF was at ₹4,600 crores against ₹2,210 crores in Q2 FY26 and ₹5,721 crores for the half year. If we look at the Q2 walk, PBT before exceptional items stood at ₹2,660 crores and non-cash items was around ₹389 crores. Tax was ₹762 crores against ₹337 crores in Q2 last year. And as I said, at the full-year results, tax is now a recurring item for us, and it will scale with profit. That gives us a cash profit after tax of ₹2,287 crores for Q2, which is up 26% YoY. Capex was ₹483 crores, broadly in line with last year and with plan. Working capital released ₹2,679 crore in this quarter. With that, payable and acceptances released around ₹4,786 crore on the back of a strong volume ramp-up, while inventories absorbed around ₹1,717 crore and receivable around ₹622 crore, both of which reflect the build for the Indonesia order and the higher run rate going into the festive season. I would want to mention here that part of this working capital release is timing-related and will partially reverse as payables normalize as we move forward.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · RANJAN KUMAR
chunks.text: Investment spending. Total Investment spending in Q2 was ₹597 crores against ₹686 crores in Q2 FY26, taking the half-year to around ₹1,112 crore. Research and development in Q2 was ₹339 crores, ₹209 crore capitalized and ₹130 crore expensed. For H1, R&D was ₹616 crores. Capital and other investments were ₹258 crores in Q2 and ₹496 crore for the half year. At approximately 2.5% of revenue, this remains comfortably within our guided range of 2% to 4%, and we continue to invest steadily in line with plan.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · RANJAN KUMAR
chunks.text: Coming to consolidated financials. The consolidated revenue for Q2 was ₹25,300 crores, up 36% YoY. EBITDA was ₹2,800 crores, up 31% at a margin of 10.9%, down 40 bps. EBIT margin was 8.9%, up to 20 basis points. So, at the consolidated level, we have actually expanded EBIT margin supported by operating leverage and share of profits from JVs and associates. Profit before tax before exceptional items was ₹1,800 crores against a loss of ₹550 crore in Q2 FY26. The comparison is distorted by the mark-to-market on our investment in Tata Capital. Excluding the mark-to-market, underlying PBT grew strongly and in line with the standalone trend. Consolidated free cash flow was ₹3,000 crores against ₹2,000 crores in Q2 FY26. Net cash stood at ₹15,900 crores as at September 30 against ₹13,700 crores at March end, which includes Tata Motors Finance Holding gross debt net of the market value of its investment in Tata Capital. This puts us at a very strong liquidity position going forward in H2 FY27. With that, let me hand this over to Girish to take you through the business update. Over to you, Girish.

So overall, our H1 VAHAN market share stands at 36.2%, which is 110 basis points higher than the FY26 level, reflecting an improvement in overall market position on a YoY basis. In Heavy Commercial Vehicles, we continue to maintain a strong leadership

Then coming to SCV pickups, the trajectory has been positive, with H1 market share improving to 27.6%. So, it is an increase of 130 basis points over FY26. chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · RANJAN KUMAR
chunks.text:
Moving on. Regarding fleet utilization, this is our internal data using the Fleet Edge, and fleet utilization remained broadly stable to improving gradually during the quarter, indicating sustained operating intensity across the fleet. The freight rates also strengthened during Q2, providing support to transporter economics. From our discussions with the transporters, the profitability had seen some pressure at the beginning of the quarter post the diesel price increase, but gradually through the quarter it has started to recover. So, looking at all these together, the utilization, freight rates, and the recovery in transporter profitability indicate a relatively stable operating environment for the fleet operators.
Let me now talk about the industry. Q2 saw healthy momentum in the Commercial Vehicle industry with industry offtake growing 28.4% year-on-year while our volumes grew at 30.5%. Freight activity remained robust through the quarter, recovering from the monsoon-led slowdown in July, supported by stronger infrastructure execution, improved mining output, festive inventory stocking, and automotive dispatches. The broader operating indicators remain supportive, with healthy E-way bill generation reflecting increased goods movement and consumption demand, and the fleet utilization improved progressively through the quarter.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · RANJAN KUMAR
chunks.text: As we enter H2, the underlying demand environment still remains healthy, supported by, of course, at an overall level, the GDP growth, but therefore that leading to increased freight availability, stable fleet utilization, infrastructure activity, and consumption-led movement. Beyond the near term, we remain positive on the structural outlook of the CV industry, which is supported by the economic growth and therefore increasing road freight, infrastructure development, and the replacement demand.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · RANJAN KUMAR
chunks.text: Talking of the specific businesses. So, the key takeaway from Q2 is that the growth momentum was broad- based across the portfolio, with healthy performance across trucks, the passenger carriers, and small commercial vehicles, alongside strong progress in our international business as also the downstream businesses. International business was a strong growth contributor during the quarter, with volumes growing 177% year-on-year, mainly supported by the Indonesia order as well as the momentum across our other international segment. In Parts & Services, we continued the healthy trajectory, sustaining growth in the aftermarket business, improving spare parts penetration, and strengthening the customer uptime proposition. Our digital business is also progressing well with FleetEdge renewal rates improving, thereby strengthening the recurring digital revenue opportunity. The e-bus operations in Smart City also continue to scale while maintaining more than 95% fleet uptime across the major operating fleets, demonstrating the progress we are making in building this business. Coming to sustainability, the EV momentum built further and remained strong in Q2 with overall EV volumes growing 143% year-on-year. Within this, the small commercial vehicle EV retails crossed 4,400

EV Trucks continue to see improving customer traction and adoption. In e-buses, as I mentioned in Smart City, the operations continue to do well with more than 95% uptime, and we have now covered more than 64 crore green kilometres since inception. So overall, the quarter saw broad-based momentum across the core vehicle businesses, international business, downstream businesses, and EVs, with the focus remaining on disciplined execution and profitable growth.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · RANJAN KUMAR
chunks.text: Now looking ahead in Q3 and maybe beyond, our priority is to leverage the healthy demand momentum while balancing pricing, cost efficiency, and supply readiness to drive profitable growth. In trucks, we will capitalize on healthy demand through portfolio actions focused on improving customer productivity, payload, and the total cost of ownership. In CV Passenger, we will capture opportunities across institutional and passenger mobility, including state transport, school and staff transportation, while progressively scaling electric buses. In SCV pickups, we will build on the portfolio enhancement and increasing EV adoption supported by resilient last-mile and e-commerce demand. In Parts & Services, the priority is to build a larger and more resilient aftermarket business by improving customer uptime offerings and expanding service reach. In international business, we will continue to diversify and scale across geographies while maintaining disciplined execution across channels, products, and markets while navigating geopolitical volatility. On IVECO, consolidation will begin next quarter, with immediate priority being to ensure a seamless transition. Overall, the Q3 agenda is about sustaining growth momentum while maintaining discipline on profitability, execution, and readiness for the next phase of the business. Thank you. So, I think that's what we see as the likely demand growth.

On the SCV Pick up front, we launched the Ace Gold+ XL, Intra V40 and Intra EV, broadening the SCV PU portfolio across ICE, CNG and electric. We also crossed a major milestone, with our Lucknow plant crossing 10 lakh commercial vehicles in cumulative production. We also partnered with HPCL on a scalable circular economy model for used automotive lubricants; and the Tata Motors Foundation's Integrated Village Development Programme has now reached close to 200 villages nationwide.
Next slide please.
There were two significant corporate actions in the quarter. On the Iveco transaction - regulatory approvals are now in the final stage, with only one approval pending. All information requests have been addressed, and we expect final clearance by the end of August 2026.

As a result, the EV volumes grew almost three times on a YoY basis. In fact, in SCV pickup, the EV penetration reached double-digit in the months of both May and June, and that continues to improve further as we get into Q2. On EV trucks, both the heavy commercial vehicle tractors and tippers, there is a very strong interest from the customer, robust engagement, and the customers are looking forward for these kinds of decarbonizing solutions. So, Jay, I mentioned this last time also, it is very difficult to differentiate between replacement demand and new vehicle purchase, so to say. But generally, what happens is large fleet owners are the first ones to replace their existing trucks in four to six years, and they go for newer trucks because they see a clear TCO benefit with the newer trucks. But at the same time, their existing trucks don't move out of the system, but they are sold to maybe smaller customers, individual vehicle owners, and they then put those vehicles to use on shorter distances. So, I think overall the demand is going up, which means there is an increase in the freight which is available and the capacity utilization of the fleet also remains strong. So, as I said, very difficult to give a separation between replacement demand, new vehicle demand. It is actually a combination of both.

Sneha Gavankar Good evening. Welcome to Tata Motors Q4 and Full Year FY26 Results Call. I have with me Mr. Girish Wagh, Managing Director and CEO, G.V. Ramanan, CFO, and the Investor Relations team. Go to the next slide, please. Before we get into the numbers, a quick word on the presentation format. Demerger being effective from 1st of October 2025, Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company, and this is a defining shift that changes how we think is most appropriate to present our financials. Historically, we reported a CV segment. It was an internal construct that carved out CV operations from within the erstwhile combined entity. That was a practical necessity then. Starting this quarter, we are presenting standalone financials, including joint operations with Tata Cummins as our primary lens. This gives you a cleaner, more complete, and more directly comparable picture of the business going forward. Operating segment, namely the CV segment comprising TML and its subsidiaries, is now included in the consolidated financial statements. Go to the next page, please. FY26 is a year of strong execution across product, market and strategic initiatives. Now the key highlights included - We launched 17 new next-generation trucks at the start of Q4, and earlier in the year, around June, we launched the Ace Pro, which is positioned as India's most affordable four-wheel mini truck.

The underlining demand trajectory has been firmly upward. While I'm really pleased with the margin story, EBITDA margins have expanded from 7.8% in FY23 to 13.2% in FY26. What I also want to draw your attention to is the chart we're particularly proud of is the bottom left panel on non-cyclical revenue growth. Business Overview — Q1 FY27
INDUSTRY BUSINESSES SUSTAINABILITY
Q1 saw healthy momentum with offtake TIV growing 18.0% YoY, and TML volumes growing 26% YoY.
Trucks: YoY market share gains with volume growth led by new product launches.
With launch of Intra EV, and 55T EV, along with tailwind of higher diesel prices, EV volumes grew 277% on a YoY basis. EV penetration reached ~10% in SCVPU in May and June.
Buses and Vans: Market share gains driven by higher retails and delivery of Govt tenders won in previous quarters.
E-way bill generation shows consistent growth of 12.4% in Q1 FY27 over Q1 FY26, signaling resilient goods movement and domestic trade activity during the quarter.
3.2K
Won orders for 562 units in Q1 FY27 across government, institutional, and STU segments. SCVPU: Ace Diesel LNT and Ace Pro ramp-up supporting volume growth.
SCV EV retails in Q1 FY27, registering ~4x YoY growth.
EV Trucks: Continued improvement in traction with increasing interest and orders in hand.
Fleet utilization : Utilization levels showed month on month improvement during Q1
Intra EV and Bi-fuel variants launched to strengthen the portfolio.
850+
EV Buses order in hand. Diesel consumption grew ~2.8% in Q1 FY27, indicating a stable demand trend.

EV Buses order in hand. Diesel consumption grew ~2.8% in Q1 FY27, indicating a stable demand trend.
Parts & Services business continued the growth trajectory in Q1. Uninterrupted DEF supplies ensured overcoming supply chain challenges arising out of Middle East crisis.
59+ Cr
Digital: Fleet Edge installed base grew to 1.1 Mn vehicles. Subscription renewal performance improved YoY.

Looking Ahead
Q2 Focus Areas:
• Overall: Manage commodity inflation through price increases and cost management. Address supply chain challenges through targeted debottlenecking in view of increased industry demand.
• Trucks: Accelerate growth through the MY26 portfolio, higher-payload trucks, and BEV expansion.
• CV Passenger: Execute ~4.5k Government, Defence and STU orders, including 850 e-buses, while sustaining Magic and tender momentum.
• SCVPU: Build on Ace and Intra momentum, leverage shift towards EVs to drive market share gains.
• Parts & Services: Accelerate year-on-year growth through demand generation, portfolio expansion and resilient supply chain fulfillment.

• Parts & Services: Accelerate year-on-year growth through demand generation, portfolio expansion and resilient supply chain fulfillment.
• International Business: Increased demand generation from other markets in view of Middle East crisis. Further ramp up of deliveries of Indonesia order.
